properties.description:

strong winds, low relative humidity, and warm temperatures can
contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued June 19 at 1:23PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...The South Coast AQMD has extended an air quality alert due
to harmful levels of fine particle pollution.
Visit https://www.aqmd.gov/alertinfo to check current and forecasted
air quality levels.

* WHERE...Boyle Heights and East Los Angeles. Levels of particle
pollution can vary by time and location depending on emissions and
local weather conditions.

* WHEN...until 12:30 PM Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Particle pollution can get deep into the lungs and cause
serious health problems such as heart attacks, bronchitis, asthma
attacks, and difficulty breathing. Everyone can be affected, but
sensitive groups such as people with lung or heart disease, older
adults, people who are pregnant, children, and those who spend a lot
of time outdoors are at greater risk.
properties.instruction:
To protect your health, check air quality levels and act as needed:

* When Air Quality Index (AQI) levels are "Unhealthy for
Sensitive Groups" (orange), sensitive groups as specified
above should limit extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Unhealthy" (red), everyone may experience health
impacts. Sensitive groups should avoid extended time outdoors.
* When AQI is "Very Unhealthy" (purple), sensitive groups should
avoid all outdoor physical activity. Everyone else should
avoid extended or intense outdoor activity.
* When AQI is "Hazardous" (maroon), everyone should avoid all
outdoor physical activity.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

To help keep indoor air clean when air quality is poor:

* Keep windows and doors closed
* Run your air conditioner and/or an air purifier
* Do not use whole house fans or swamp coolers that bring in
outside air if you have other methods to stay cool
* Avoid other sources of pollution such as fireplaces, candles,
incense, grilling, and gasoline-powered lawn and garden
equipment
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

Weather Service and area fire management agencies.

properties.description:
...The Flood Warning is extended for the following rivers in
Mississippi...

Biloxi River Near Lyman affecting Harrison County.

For the Biloxi River...including Wortham, Lyman...Major flooding is
forecast.

* WHAT...Major flooding is occurring and major flooding is forecast.
This approaches the flood of record.

* WHERE...Biloxi River near Lyman.

* WHEN...Until Monday evening.

* IMPACTS...At 21.0 feet, Flood of Record occurred on May 10, 1995.
Major flooding will occur along the river. Several bridges and
roads may be washed out. Evacuation of Biloxi River Estates,
Retreat Village, Oakridge Manor, Rolling Acres, and Riverland
Village is strongly recommended. Sections of MS Highway 605 will be
impassable.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 12:45 PM CDT Friday the stage was 21.2 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 9.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 12:45 PM CDT Friday was 21.2 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to fall below flood stage early
Monday afternoon and continue falling to 6.7 feet Wednesday
morning.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 21.0
feet on 05/10/1995.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Motorists should not attempt to drive around barricades or drive cars
through flooded areas.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/lix.  Click on
the Rivers and Lakes menu for forecasts and observations.

The next statement will be issued when updates are needed.

potentially extreme fire behavior.

Warning in effect from noon to 7 PM MDT Saturday.

Mountains (Zone 105), North Central Mountains (Zone 120), and Upper

* IMPACTS...Any fires that develop will spread rapidly. Outdoor
burning is not recommended.

properties.headline: Lakeshore Flood Warning issued June 19 at 11:04AM EDT until June 19 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Buffalo NY
properties.description:
* WHAT...Minor lakeshore flooding.

* WHERE...Lake Ontario shore of Oswego and Jefferson counties.
Elevated water levels are also possible along the upper Saint
Lawrence River in the Thousand Islands region.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM EDT this evening.

* IMPACTS...The combination of high lake levels and significant
wave action will result in minor lakeshore flooding along the
immediate lakeshore, especially in bays, inlets, harbors, and
other low lying areas along the shoreline. Shoreline erosion
is also expected.
properties.instruction:
A Lakeshore Flood Warning means lakeshore flooding is occurring,
is imminent, or is expected to occur. For your safety, stay off
breakwaters, piers, rock outcroppings and beaches! Waves are
often larger than they appear and can easily wash you away.
Expect significant beach erosion and debris, local road closures
and extremely dangerous boating conditions.

properties.headline: Flood Warning issued June 19 at 9:57AM CDT until June 20 at 6:00PM CDT by NWS Lake Charles LA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Urban area and small stream flooding caused by excessive
rainfall will continue.

* WHERE...A portion of central Louisiana, including the following
parish, St. Landry.

* WHEN...Until 600 PM CDT Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying
and flood-prone locations is imminent or occurring. Numerous roads
remain closed due to flooding. Streams continue to rise due to
excess runoff from earlier rainfall. Expect many areas of slow
moving or standing water. It will take several hours for all the
water from these storms to work through local drainage systems in
urban areas.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 957 AM CDT, emergency management reported heavy rain in
the warned area due to runoff and standing water from
previous excessive rainfall. Flooding is already occurring.
Between 5 and 29 inches of rain have fallen.
- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Krotz Springs, Melville, Palmetto, Bayou Current, Morrow,
Port Barre, Washington, Lebeau, Big Cane, Grand Prairie and
Whiteville.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Keep children away from storm drains, culverts, creeks and streams.
Water levels can rise rapidly and sweep children away.

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued June 19 at 9:52PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
THE NEAR-EQUATORIAL TROUGH (NET) HAS BECOME VERY ACTIVE ACROSS
EASTERN MICRONESIA, WITH NUMEROUS TO WIDESPREAD HEAVY SHOWERS SOUTH
OF POHNPEI AND OVER KOSRAE. A WEAK DISTURBANCE, INVEST 93W, HAS ALSO
FORMED ALONG THE NET NEAR 10N160E. THE NET AND ASSOCIATED CONVECTION
LOOK TO DRIFT NORTHWARD OVER THE NEXT FEW DAYS, AS INVEST 93W SLOWLY
MOVES WEST-NORTHWEST. LITTLE DEVELOPMENT IS EXPECTED WITH 93W AS IT
MOVES OUT, HOWEVER, IT WILL HELP INCREASE RAINFALL POTENTIAL ACROSS
THE REGION.

POHNPEI AND KOSRAE COULD SEE RAINFALL AMOUNTS OF 5 TO 10 INCHES
THROUGH THE WEEKEND, WITH LOCALLY HEAVIER AMOUNTS POSSIBLE. THIS
AMOUNT OF RAINFALL WILL LEAD TO FLOODING, LOCALIZED FLASH FLOODING
AND POSSIBLE MUDSLIDES OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL DAYS. THE HEAVY
RAINFALL WILL ALSO RESULT IN REDUCED VISIBILITIES, MAKING TRAVEL
DANGEROUS. USE CAUTION WHEN TRAVELING OVER THE NEXT SEVERAL DAYS.
THE NET IS SHOWING THE POTENTIAL TO REMAIN ACTIVE INTO THE MIDDLE OF
NEXT WEEK, POSSIBLY RESULTING IN A PROLONGED PERIOD OF HEAVY RAINS,
INCREASING THE MUDSLIDE POTENTIAL.

RESIDENTS OF POHNPEI AND KOSRAE SHOULD REMAIN ALERT FOR HEAVY
RAINFALL, FLOOD AND MUDSLIDES WATCHES, WARNINGS OR ADVISORIES ISSUED
BY YOUR LOCAL NATIONAL WEATHER SERVICE OFFICES. HEED THE ADVICE OF
LOCAL EMERGENCY MANAGERS. THOSE WHO LIVE IN FLOOD PRONE AREAS SHOULD
WORK TO SECURE AND SAFEGUARD PROPERTY.

properties.areaDesc: Chuuk Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued June 19 at 9:51PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
The Near-Equatorial Trough (NET) has become very active across
eastern Micronesia, with numerous to widespread heavy showers
extending south of Chuuk. A weak disturbance, Invest 93W, has also
formed along the NET near 10N160E. The NET and associated convection
look to drift northward over the next few days, as Invest 93W slowly
moves west- northwest. Little development is expected with 93W as it
moves out, however, it will help increase rainfall potential across
the region.

Weno could see rainfall amounts of 5 to 10 inches through the
weekend, with locally heavier amounts possible. This amount of
rainfall will lead to flooding, localized flash flooding and possible
mudslides over the next several days. The heavy rainfall will also
result in reduced visibilities, making travel dangerous. Use caution
when traveling over the next several days. The NET is showing the
potential to remain active into the middle of next week, possibly
resulting in a prolonged period of heavy rains, increasing the
mudslide potential.

Residents of Chuuk should remain alert for heavy rainfall, flood and
mudslides watches, warnings or advisories issued by your local
National Weather Service office. Heed the advice of local Emergency
Managers. Those who live in flood prone areas should work to secure
and safeguard property.

properties.headline: Beach Hazards Statement issued June 19 at 3:53AM EDT until June 19 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Newport/Morehead City NC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents, large breaking waves expected,
and strong longshore currents in the surf zone.

* WHERE...For the dangerous rip currents, large breaking waves,
and strong longshore currents, the beaches from Cape Hatteras
to Surf City. For the strong longshore currents, the beaches
from Oregon Inlet to Cape Hatteras.

* WHEN...From 8 AM EDT Friday through Friday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water. Dangerous shore break can throw
a swimmer or surfer head first into the bottom causing neck
and back injuries. Strong longshore currents will create
dangerous swimming conditions.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The most likely time for strong rip
currents to occur is a couple hours either side of low tide,
which will occur around 5:00 PM Friday.
properties.instruction:
Life-threatening rip currents. If caught in a rip current, remain
calm. Swim in a direction following the shoreline. If tired,
float or tread water until out of the rip current. If unable to
escape, face the shore and call or wave for help.

Shore break occurs when waves break directly on the beach. It is
extremely important to protect your head and neck whenever you
are in breaking waves by keeping your hands in front of you at
all times.

Strong longshore currents can sweep swimmers and surfers into rip
currents, piers, jetties and other hazardous areas. In many
cases, the longshore current is strong enough to prevent swimmers
from being able to keep their feet on the bottom making it
difficult to return to shore.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued June 18 at 10:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Thursday June 18 to 400 PM Friday June 19

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  However, hot and stagnant weather will
allow ozone to reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups category
on Thursday and Friday.  For Colorado air quality conditions,
forecasts, and advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Friday, June 19, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone pollution
through state policies. For more information about health impacts
and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

properties.headline: Air Quality Alert issued June 18 at 4:10PM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
The Colorado Department of Public Health and Environment has
issued the following...

WHAT...Ozone Action Day Alert.

WHERE...Douglas, Jefferson, Denver, western Arapahoe, western
Adams, Broomfield, Boulder, Larimer, and Weld Counties

WHEN...400 PM Thursday June 18 to 400 PM Friday June 19

IMPACTS...Ozone Action Day Alert is now in effect for the Front
Range Urban Corridor.  However, hot and stagnant weather will
allow ozone to reach the Unhealthy for Sensitive Groups category
on Thursday and Friday.  For Colorado air quality conditions,
forecasts, and advisories, visit:
https://www.colorado.gov/airquality/colorado_summary.aspx   If
possible, please help us reduce ozone pollution by limiting
driving gas and diesel-powered vehicles until at least 4 p.m.
Friday, June 19, 2026. Colorado is also addressing ozone pollution
through state policies. For more information about health impacts
and how ozone pollution forms in Colorado, visit:
https://cdphe.colorado.gov/ozone- pollution-and-your-health

HEALTH INFORMATION...Increasing likelihood of respiratory symptoms
and breathing discomfort in active children and adults and people
with lung disease, such as asthma. Active children and adults, and
people with lung disease, such as asthma, should reduce prolonged
or heavy outdoor exertion.
properties.note: Non-Weather Emergency Message. Not sent to IPAWS.

NWSheadline: OZONE ACTION DAY ALERT FROM 400 PM THURSDAY UNTIL 400 PM FRIDAY

properties.headline: Fire Weather Watch issued June 18 at 1:49PM AKDT until June 21 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
The National Weather Service in Fairbanks has issued a Fire
Weather Watch for lightning, which is in effect from Saturday
morning through Sunday evening.

* AFFECTED AREA...White Mountains, Tanana Valley, Chena River
Valley, Fortymile Country, and Eastern Delta Junction.

* TIMING...From Saturday morning through Sunday evening.

* THUNDERSTORM COVERAGE INDEX...Scattered.

* WINDS...Near thunderstorms, gusts could reach as high as 40
mph.

* HUMIDITY...As low as 30 percent.

* TEMPERATURES...Highs in the low 80s. Lows in the low 50s.

* IMPACTS...Critical fire weather conditions are possible this
weekend due to a combination of thunderstorm activity,
temperatures reaching into the low 80s, relative humidities
near 30 percent, and gusty winds.
properties.instruction:
A Fire Weather Watch means that weather conditions could lead to
the potential for a Red Flag event in the near future. This watch
will remain in effect until it is upgraded to a Red Flag Warning
or that it is determined that the Red Flag event will not
develop.

Please advise the appropriate officials or fire crews in the
field of this Fire Weather Watch.

NWSheadline: FIRE WEATHER WATCH REMAINS IN EFFECT FROM SATURDAY MORNING THROUGH SUNDAY EVENING FOR LIGHTNING

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued June 18 at 1:47PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
On Friday through Sunday, a majority of the Central and Eastern
Interior will see multiple days of highs near/above 80 degrees
Fahrenheit. Take caution while participating in outdoor
activities planned for the solstice/holiday weekend. Stay hydrated
and limit strenuous outdoor activities in the afternoon when
temperatures are highest.

NWSheadline: Hot Temperatures in the Interior This Weekend

properties.areaDesc: Yukon Flats
properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued June 18 at 1:27PM AKDT until June 21 at 10:00PM AKDT by NWS Fairbanks AK
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot temperatures as high as 85 expected.

* WHERE...Yukon Flats.

* WHEN...From 1 PM Friday to 10 PM AKDT Sunday.

* IMPACTS...Individuals not accustomed to these hot temperatures may
experience heat related illnesses.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Temperatures will reach their peak during
each afternoon from Friday through Sunday. Temperatures overnight
will provide some relief but remain warm, around 55 to 65.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids and check up on elderly and vulnerable
relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when working in the sun. Wear sunscreen and
lightweight, loose fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous
activities to early morning or late evening. Take action when you
see symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat stroke.

Close curtains during the daytime to reduce sun insolation into the
home and open windows at night to allow the home to cool off.
Utilize fans or community buildings with air conditioning.
